docs.text: Welcome to TR-Scripts ! We offer high-quality, custom-made RedM scripts, primarily for the VORP framework. We're proud to create clean, efficient scripts. We aim to make all of our scripts feel like they should've been built into the game this entire time. To get started, pick a script from the sidebar. Most of our scripts are built using jo_libs . Questions? Check out our Discord server for support.

docs.text: Players walk up to a bench, a campfire or a stove, pick a recipe from a menu, and craft it with a short key-press minigame while their character works. Works on any framework jo_libs supports. A few extras (weapon names and stack limits) are read from VORP when it's installed. How it works ¶ Walking up to a crafting spot shows a prompt. Pressing it walks the player up to the bench (or turns them to face the campfire) and opens the menu: The first page lists the categories. If a location only has one category the player can use, the menu opens straight into it. Each category is a grid of recipes. A recipe shows what it needs, how much of each ingredient you have, and its stack limit. Recipes you can't make are greyed out. A recipe with several ways of paying has a Pay with slider (Q / E) instead. Picking a recipe starts crafting. You make one per round of the minigame, as many times as your ingredients allow. Failing a round or pressing Escape stops early, keeping whatever you already made. At the end you get a summary, and the menu updates to show what's left. Everything is checked again on the server before anything is crafted: the job and grade, the ingredients or money, and whether the result fits in the inventory. If it doesn't fit, everything paid is given back. Requirements ¶ jo_libs oxmysql A framework and inventory supported by jo_libs (VORP, RSG, RedEM:RP, ...)

docs.text: Put tr-crafting in your resources folder. Add it to server.cfg after its dependencies: ensure oxmysql ensure jo_libs ensure vorp_inventory # or your framework's inventory ensure tr-crafting Set up your locations and recipes in the config (see Configuration ). Every item used in a recipe, both ingredients and outputs, must exist in your inventory's items list. Placeable campfire The placeable campfire uses an item called campfire by default. Add it to your items if you use it, or turn it off (see Props & field crafting ).

docs.text: General ¶ Setting What it does Config.Debug Extra logging, and the tr-crafting:testAnim command for trying animations. Config.KeyHashes Keys used for prompts. The first opens the crafting menu; the second puts out your campfire. Config.PromptDistance How close (in metres) you need to be to a spot to see the prompt. Config.PropDistance How close you need to be to a crafting prop (campfire, stove...). Config.AllowMovement Whether the player can move while the menu is open. Config.Minigame true for the key-press minigame (one round per item); false to craft once after Config.CraftTime seconds. Config.Webhook A Discord webhook for crafting logs (leave empty for none). Locations ¶ Config . CraftingLocations = { [ "carpenter" ] = { label = "Carpenter" , blip = "blip_mp_ugc" , -- leave out for no blip jobs = { -- leave out for anyone { name = "carpenter" }, -- any grade { name = "builder" , minGrade = 2 }, }, locations = { [ "strawberry" ] = vector3 ( - 1812.8 , - 426.44 , 159.95 ), [ "blackwater" ] = vector4 ( - 867.15 , - 1291.85 , 43.0 , 90.0 ), }, categories = { [ "Materials" ] = { jobs = { { name = "carpenter" , minGrade = 2 } }, -- optional: replaces the location's jobs here recipes = { [ "plank" ] = { output = { { item = "plank" } }, cost = { { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 } }, }, }, }, }, }, } locations are the spots players walk up to. Use a vector4 to make the player face a direction (the heading) when they start. jobs is a list: a player with any one of them can use it. minGrade and maxGrade are both inclusive, and either can be left out. A location can also have props (craft at any matching object) or a command (craft anywhere). See Props & field crafting . Categories with no recipes the player can see aren't shown. Animations ¶ Anims.Animations lists the animations recipes can use. Each has a dict , a name , an optional flag (default 17, which loops), and optional props the player holds: [ "hammer_kneel" ] = { dict = "amb_work@world_human_hammer@kneel@male_a@trans" , name = "base_trans_base" , props = { { model = "p_hammerclaw01x" , pos = vector3 ( 0.1 , - 0.04 , 0.22 ), rot = vector3 ( 175.0 , 20.0 , 170.0 ) }, }, }, A prop's bone defaults to the right hand ( SKEL_R_Finger13 ). A prop can have its own props that go with it, like the plank and nails in hammer_table . Text ¶ Everything players read is in lang.lua .

docs.text: Fields ¶ Field What it does output What gets made: { { item = "plank", quantity = 2 } } . A recipe can make several things. quantity defaults to 1. Leave out for an action . cost What it costs: items, money, gold or rol, or a choice of those. See Prices . Leave out for a free recipe. costLabels Names for each way of paying, shown on the Pay with slider. jobs Who can see and make it, on top of the location's and category's jobs. See Jobs . limit The most of the output a player can hold. For an action , how many times it can be done at once. animation Which animation from Anims.Animations to play. Defaults to craft . weapon true if the output is a weapon. label The name shown in the menu. Defaults to the item's name. image The image shown in the menu. Defaults to the item's image. onCraft A function run on the server after each successful craft: function(source) ... end . Prices ¶ cost takes anything jo_libs' pricing understands. Items: cost = { { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "nails" , quantity = 2 } }, Items and money together. Everything has to be paid: cost = { money = 1000 , { item = "earth_star" }, { item = "fire_rose" } }, Tools. An item with keep = true must be in the player's inventory, but isn't used up: cost = { { item = "iron" }, { item = "hammer" , keep = true } }, A choice of ways to pay. When the options are lists themselves, the player picks one with the Pay with slider in the menu (Q / E): cost = { { -- option 1 { item = "rock" , quantity = 10 }, { item = "wood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "coal" , quantity = 4 }, }, { -- option 2 { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "wood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "porkfat" , quantity = 5 }, }, }, costLabels = { "Rocks & coal" , "Hardwood & pork fat" }, The slider starts on the option the player can best afford, and only the chosen option is charged. Choices of a single cost For alternatives that are each a single cost ($10 or 1 gold), wrap each in its own list: { { { money = 10 } }, { { gold = 1 } } } . A plain list of single costs, { { item = "a" }, { item = "b" } } , means pay all of them. Jobs ¶ Jobs can be set on the location, a category and a recipe: The location's jobs decide who gets the prompt at all. A category's jobs replace the location's for that category. A recipe's jobs are checked on top , for example a higher grade for one recipe. Players without one of them don't see the recipe. [ "Lockpick" ] = { jobs = { { name = "blacksmith" , minGrade = 2 } }, output = { { item = "lockpick" } }, cost = { { item = "iron" , quantity = 3 }, { item = "copper" , quantity = 2 } }, }, Actions ¶ A recipe with no output that runs an onCraft is an action : boiling a canteen, cleaning something. Give it a label , since there's no item to take its name from: [ "BoilCanteen" ] = { label = "Boil Canteen" , cost = { { item = "canteen" , keep = true } }, limit = 1 , -- once at a time onCraft = function ( source ) -- fill or clean the canteen here end , }, The summary uses the label: "You crafted 1x Boil Canteen." Weapons and stack limits ¶ jo_libs doesn't provide weapon names or stack limits, so: On VORP, weapon names and images come from vorp_inventory/config/weapons.lua , and stack limits from the items table. tr-crafting waits for vorp_inventory to start, and reloads them when it restarts. On other frameworks, weapons show a name made from their code ( WEAPON_FISHINGROD becomes "Fishingrod"), and there are no stack limits unless you set limit on the recipe. Weapons are given with VORP's own weapon function on VORP, and as normal items ( weapon_fishingrod ) elsewhere.

docs.text: Crafting at props ¶ A location can have props instead of (or as well as) fixed spots. The prompt then shows next to any matching object in the world, titled with that object's name: [ "campfire" ] = { label = "Campfire" , props = { -- [model] = prompt title [ "p_campfire05x" ] = "Campfire" , [ "p_stove04x" ] = "Stove" , }, categories = { ... }, }, The player turns to face the object instead of walking to a spot. Keep the list short: tr-crafting checks for each model near the player every half second. The placeable campfire ¶ Using the campfire item places a campfire in front of the player. Its model is a crafting prop like any other (add it to a location's props ), and whoever placed it gets a Put Out prompt. Config . PlaceableCampfire = { item = "campfire" , -- leave out to turn this off model = "p_campfire05x" , animation = "campfire" , -- while lighting it placeTime = 4000 , -- ms max = 1 , -- how many one player can have burning burnTime = 30 , -- minutes until it burns out (0 = until put out) -- jobs = { { name = "hunter" } }, } The item is taken before the fire is placed, so a campfire is never free. Field crafting ¶ A location with no spots can be opened anywhere, with a command : [ "field" ] = { label = "Crafting" , command = "crafting" , -- /crafting opens it categories = { ... }, }, Or from another script, on the client: exports [ "tr-crafting" ]: openCrafting ( "field" )

docs.text: Other resources can add locations, spots, categories and recipes from their server scripts, in the same format as the config: local crafting = exports [ "tr-crafting" ] -- a recipe at an existing location (the category is created if needed) crafting : addRecipe ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" , { output = { { item = "chair" } }, cost = { { item = "plank" , quantity = 4 }, { item = "nails" , quantity = 8 } }, }) -- a whole location crafting : addLocation ( "blacksmith" , { label = "Blacksmith" , jobs = { { name = "blacksmith" } }, locations = { valentine = vector4 ( - 367.0 , 787.0 , 116.2 , 90.0 ) }, categories = { Metal = { recipes = { nails = { output = { { item = "nails" , quantity = 10 } }, cost = { { item = "iron" } } } } }, }, }) -- another spot for an existing location crafting : addPoint ( "carpenter" , "rhodes" , vector3 ( 1340.2 , - 1300.5 , 77.0 )) -- add to (or create) a category crafting : addCategory ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , { jobs = { { name = "carpenter" , minGrade = 2 } } }) -- remove a recipe, a category, or a whole location crafting : remove ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" ) crafting : remove ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" ) crafting : remove ( "blacksmith" ) Adding something that already exists replaces it. Each export returns true , or false with a warning in the server console. When the resource that added something stops, its additions are removed, and anything it replaced is put back. Registering on start ¶ Restarting tr-crafting reloads its config, so anything added by other scripts is lost. Add yours again whenever tr-crafting starts: local function register () exports [ "tr-crafting" ]: addRecipe ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" , { ... }) end AddEventHandler ( "onResourceStart" , function ( resource ) if resource == "tr-crafting" then register () end end ) if GetResourceState ( "tr-crafting" ) == "started" then register () end Opening a menu ¶ On the client, exports["tr-crafting"]:openCrafting(key) opens a location's menu where the player is. It returns false if the location doesn't exist, the player doesn't have its job, or a menu is already open.

docs.text: A recipe offers "1 of 99" when it should allow fewer ¶ 99 is the cap for recipes whose costs never run out (only tools, or free). Stack limits should stop it sooner. Check that the item has a limit in VORP's items table, or set limit on the recipe. With Config.Debug = true , the server console shows how many stack limits were loaded on start. Item [nil] does not exist in DB ¶ A recipe with no output (an action) is fine. If you see this, check your recipes for ingredients or outputs written in the old VORP format, { name = "...", count = 1 } , instead of { item = "..." } . If it only appears when a particular item arrives in an inventory, another script is reacting to that item. A weapon shows a plain name, or no image ¶ Weapon names come from VORP's weapons config. On other frameworks, set label and image on the recipe. Recipes added by another script disappear ¶ They're lost when tr-crafting restarts. Register them on start: see For developers .

docs.text: A fast job assignment and switching system for RedM. A character can hold several jobs at once, each at its own grade, and switch between them. Jobs belong to a family (for example, every saloon job is in the saloon family), so scripts can check for a kind of job rather than every job by name. Requirements ¶ jo_libs

docs.text: All commands are server-side only: run them from the server console. getjobs [playerID] ¶ Lists all of a player's job assignments. getjobs 1 [ { "job" : { "grade" : 1 , "family" : "carpenter" , "name" : "carpenter" , "id" : 64 , "label" : "Carpenter" }, "id" : 166 , "charid" : 1 , "lastactive" : "07/24/2026" , "created" : "07/24/2026" }, { "job" : { "grade" : 1 , "family" : "saloon" , "name" : "blackwaterbordello" , "id" : 24 , "label" : "Blackwater Bordello" }, "id" : 168 , "charid" : 1 , "lastactive" : "07/24/2026" , "created" : "07/24/2026" } ] createjob [name] [grade] [family] [label...] ¶ Creates a new job. Everything after the family is the label, so it can have spaces. createjob doctor 3 medical Associate Doctor tr-jobs: job created with id: 46 addjob [playerID] [name] [grade] ¶ Gives a player a job. addjob 1 carpenter 1 removejob [playerID] [name] [grade] ¶ Takes a job away from a player. removejob 1 leo 2

docs.text: tr-jobs answers questions through jo_libs callbacks . Call them with jo.callback.triggerServer , either with a function that receives the answer later, or without one to wait for the answer. Calling from the server From a client, the server knows who's asking. From the server , there's no player behind the request, so pass the player's ID yourself, as the first value. If you leave it out, the next value you pass (a job name, say) is taken as the player. tr-jobs:getCurrentJob ¶ The player's current job and grade. -- client local job , grade = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getCurrentJob" ) jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getCurrentJob" , function ( job , grade ) -- ... end ) -- server local job , grade = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getCurrentJob" , source ) jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getCurrentJob" , function ( job , grade ) -- ... end , source ) tr-jobs:getMyJobs ¶ All of the player's job assignments, as a table (the same as getjobs ). -- client local assignments = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getMyJobs" ) -- server local assignments = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getMyJobs" , source ) tr-jobs:getPlayersWithJob ¶ Every player with a job at a grade. -- client local players = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getPlayersWithJob" , job , grade ) -- server (0 stands in for the player asking) local players = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getPlayersWithJob" , 0 , job , grade ) tr-jobs:getJobFamily ¶ The family of the player's current job. -- client local family = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getJobFamily" ) -- server local family = jo . callback . triggerServer ( "tr-jobs:getJobFamily" , source )

docs.text: A writable journal for RedM. Players open a leather-bound journal, give it a title, and write page by page. Pages can be torn out to keep, give away, or pass as notes, and each torn page is its own readable item. Features ¶ A leather-bound journal with ruled cream pages and a handwritten font, opened from the inventory. A title at the top of the journal, which also becomes the journal's name in the inventory, so journals are easy to tell apart. Multiple pages , turned with Prev and Next , up to the number of pages a journal holds. Tear out a page to get it as a torn_page item. The page is only torn out if the player has room for it in their inventory, so nothing is ever lost. Torn pages open as a single sheet with a torn edge, readable by whoever holds them. A writing animation while the journal is open, and a reading animation with a sheet of paper in hand for torn pages. An optional screen filter while reading or writing. The journal and the torn page can be dragged around the screen. Saved automatically when the journal is closed. Requirements ¶ VORP Core and VORP Inventory oxmysql jo_libs , with the framework and notif modules

docs.text: Writing in a journal ¶ Use a journal_blank or journal_written from the inventory to open it. The mouse appears, and your character starts writing. Title: the line at the top. It's also the journal's name in the inventory (up to 30 characters). Writing: click the page and type. Tab indents. Prev / Next: turn the pages. Page 3 of 50 shows where you are, and how many pages the journal has. X (top right) or Esc: close the journal. It saves. While the journal is open, the game's controls are paused apart from push-to-talk, so you can type freely. The first time a blank journal is closed, it becomes a written journal ( journal_written ), named after its title. This needs room in the inventory for the written journal: if there's none, the journal stays blank and what was written isn't saved , so make room first. Tearing out a page ¶ Tear Page (top left) tears out the page you're on. It's greyed out on an empty page. If you have room, the page leaves the journal and goes into your inventory as a torn_page , and the journal closes and saves. If your inventory is full, you're told there's no room, and the journal is saved with the page still in it . Tearing out a journal's last page uses up the journal: it's removed from your inventory. Reading a torn page ¶ Use a torn_page to read it. Its inventory description shows the start of what's written on it. Close it with X or Esc . Good to know ¶ A journal belongs to the item, not the character: whoever holds that journal_written item can open and write in it, so journals can be given, traded, or found. Journals and the torn page can be dragged by any part that isn't text or a button.

docs.text: A post office system for RedM: rent mailboxes, send telegrams, letters and packages, and let a mail carrier job deliver the post between towns. Features ¶ Mailboxes : rent a numbered box (e.g. #0042 ) at any post office, name it, share keys with other players or a whole trade, and transfer or close it. Telegrams : written on a telegram form and delivered to the recipient's mailbox after a short delay. Players are notified when a telegram is waiting. Letters : post any note or letter you're carrying to another mailbox number. Packages : buy a box, pack items into it, and post it. Postage depends on weight. Notes : write a note at the counter, keep it, or post it straight away. Mailbox directory : a searchable public listing of registered mailboxes. Mail carrier job : carriers collect outgoing mail at the mail desk and deliver it to other post offices, and are paid by distance. Map blips show which post offices have mail waiting for you, and (for carriers) which have mail to deliver. Post office staff : a clerk at each counter, opening hours, and a camera that turns to the clerk while you're served. Discord webhooks log mailboxes being opened, renamed, transferred and deleted, keys changing hands, mail being sent and delivered, and packages being packed and opened. Requirements ¶ VORP Core and VORP Inventory oxmysql jo_libs (menus, prompts, notifications, inputs) MySQL or MariaDB. If you're on MariaDB 11.5 or newer , use the included tr-mail.sql as-is: it already contains a fix for that version's stricter text-comparison rules.

docs.text: Walk up to a post office counter during opening hours and press the prompt. The menu has: Telegrams ¶ All telegrams waiting in any mailbox you can open, from every post office. Select one to collect it as a telegram item, then use it from your inventory to read it. Mailboxes ¶ Your mailboxes at this post office , and the mail waiting in each. Select a letter or package to take it. Open New Mailbox rents a new box at this post office (the first one is cheaper). Manage Mailbox (owners only): Rename : the name shown in the directory. Add Access : give a key to a player by their server ID, with a private nickname that only you see in your key list. Remove Access : take a key back. Register / Unregister : list or hide the box in the public directory. Set Owner : hand the box to another player. You keep access if you still hold a key, through your trade or personally. Delete : close the box. Press twice to confirm; any mail inside is destroyed . Send Mail ¶ Send Telegram : write on the telegram form and enter the recipient's 4-digit mailbox number. Send Letter : pick a note or letter you're carrying and enter the mailbox number. Send Package : pick a packed package; the price depends on its weight. Buy Box sells an empty box. Mail to a mailbox at the same post office arrives straight away. Mail to another town waits for a mail carrier to take it there. Write Note ¶ Write a note on paper (costs a small fee). It goes into your inventory as a mail_note , and is immediately available under Send Letter . Mailbox Directory ¶ Search registered mailboxes by name or number. Select one to copy its number, ready to paste when sending. Packing a package ¶ Use an empty box from your inventory. A container opens: put the items in and close it. The box becomes a package with those items inside. Whoever receives it uses the package to unpack it.

docs.text: tr-properties is the shared base for anything players can own: houses, ranches, businesses. It handles who owns what, the doors and keys, storage, map blips and property taxes. Other scripts (tr-housing, tr-ranching, tr-government) plug into it for everything else. Works on any framework jo_libs supports. Reading the keys in a player's pockets is the one inventory-specific part, and it's a single function in the config. How it works ¶ Every property is an entry in the config: a name, a price, its doors, and optionally storage and a blip. Buying. Walking up to an unowned property shows a Buy prompt with its price (or it's sold through another script, such as tr-government's office). The buyer gets a key. Keys. Keys are real items. Using one at a door locks or unlocks it, but only if that key fits the current lock. Keys can be copied, stolen and lost; changing the locks makes every old key useless. Doors. Each door listed for a property has its own lock. Interior doors you leave out aren't touched. Lockpicking. A lockpick opens (or locks) a single door, or a storage, with a minigame. No key needed. Storage. A property can have a stash, opened by anyone carrying a key that fits. Taxes. Owners are charged weekly. A property whose owner can't pay goes back on the market. Everything is checked on the server: who's standing where, which key fits, who's allowed in. Requirements ¶ jo_libs oxmysql A framework and inventory supported by jo_libs (VORP, RSG, RedEM:RP, ...)

docs.text: The property list is in config.server-only.lua and has its own page . Everything else is in config.lua . General ¶ Setting Default What it does Config.Debug false Extra logging, and the door setup commands (see Doors & keys ). Config.Webhook false A Discord webhook for purchases, transfers, lock changes, lockpicking and taxes. Config.KeyItem "key" The key item. A property type or property can use its own with keyItem . Config.OwnerNeedsKey true false lets an owner open their property without carrying a key. Config.DoorSales true Buy unowned properties at the door. Turned off automatically when another script takes over sales. Config.PromptDistance 2.0 How close (in metres) a player needs to be for the door and buy prompts. Config.SyncDistance 30.0 Doors are kept in their right state inside this range. Config.Prompts.Storage "INPUT_INTERACT_OPTION1" The key for Open Storage . Config.MaxOwned { house = 1, ranch = 1 } How many of each type one character can own. Types not listed have no limit. Config.DoorPrompt { business = true } Types that get a Lock / Unlock prompt at the door for anyone with access. Every other type uses the key item. Config.Storage { house = true, ranch = true } Types whose storage tr-properties handles. Leave a type out if another script handles its storage. Config.MasterJobs {} Jobs that can open every lockable property, e.g. { { name = "realtor" } } . Property types ¶ Defaults for every property of a type. A property can still override any of them. Config . PropertyTypes = { house = { storagePrefix = "houseID_" }, ranch = { storagePrefix = "ranchID_" , keyItem = "key_ranch" }, } Any property field works here, e.g. lockpick , storageLockpick or keyItem . Blips ¶ Config . Blips = { -- default blip per type; types not listed get none house = { sprite = "blip_proc_home" , label = "House" }, ranch = { sprite = "blip_fence_building" , label = "Ranch" }, } Config . BlipModifiers = { -- defaults for every blip forSale = "BLIP_MODIFIER_FOR_SALE" , -- unowned and has a price owned = "BLIP_MODIFIER_LOCKED" , -- owned by someone else mine = false , -- yours, or you carry a key that fits } A blip is built from Config.BlipModifiers , then Config.Blips[type] , then the property's own blip , each overriding the last. Without a label , the property's own label is used. Set false on any modifier to show none. Taxes ¶ Config . Taxes = { ChargeWeeklyTaxes = true , IntervalDays = 7 , -- days between collections GiveCharacterLienSales = true , -- pay the old owner part of the price when a property is taken LienSalesPercentage = 0.80 , TaxAmount = { -- per collection, by type; 0 or missing = no tax house = 200.0 , ranch = 500.0 , business = 0.0 , }, } Taxes are collected two minutes after the server starts, from every property that's due. If the owner can't pay, the property is released and goes back on the market, and (with GiveCharacterLienSales ) the old owner is paid LienSalesPercentage of its price. Properties owned by a job aren't taxed. The money itself is taken and paid by Config.Functions.ChargeTax and PayLienSale (below). Locksmith ¶ Config . Locksmith = { jobs = { { name = "blacksmith" , minGrade = 2 } }, cost = { { item = "iron" } }, -- per key copy or lock change locations = { -- use a key here to copy it [ "valentineBlacksmith" ] = vector3 ( - 361.21 , 802.66 , 116.16 ), }, } See Doors & keys for what a locksmith can do. Lockpicking ¶ Config . Lockpick = { item = "lockpick" , -- false turns lockpicking off distance = 1.5 , -- how close to the door timeout = 120 , -- seconds the minigame may take removeOnFail = true , -- a failed attempt uses up the lockpick relockUnowned = 30 , -- minutes until a picked door on an unowned property locks again; false = until restart storage = true , -- false: no storage can be picked; a { minigame settings } table: every storage uses those animLoop = { 0.21 , 0.53 }, -- the part of the picking animation that loops (0 = start, 1 = end) minigame = { -- jo.minigame.lockpick settings animPostFx = "OJDominoBlur" , }, } minigame takes anything jo_libs' lockpick minigame understands, e.g. pins . A door or storage can override it with its own lockpick . Functions ¶ The parts that depend on your inventory or bank live here, so you can change them without touching the script: Function What it does KeyLocks(src, item) Returns { [lockUid] = true } for every key of that item the player carries. The default reads VORP's inventory. ChargeTax(charid, amount) Takes a tax from the character's bank. Returns true if it was paid. PayLienSale(charid, amount) Pays a lien sale into the character's bank. Returns true if it was paid. The defaults for ChargeTax and PayLienSale use a tr_bank table. Replace them for your banking script.

docs.text: Properties are listed in config/config.server-only.lua , grouped by type. A property's id is <type>:<key> , e.g. house:57858 or ranch:pronghorn_ranch . Ids are stored in the database, so don't change a key once a property is in use. Config . Properties = { house = { [ 57858 ] = { label = "Winter Getaway" , price = 12000 , coords = vector3 ( - 1319.81 , 2449.77 , 309 ), doors = { [ 1073092033 ] = vector4 ( - 1319.81 , 2449.77 , 309.0 , - 25.53 ), }, storage = { coords = vector3 ( - 1317.91 , 2454.16 , 310 ), weight = 500 }, }, }, ranch = { [ "pronghorn_ranch" ] = { ... }, }, business = {}, } Types are just names: add any you like. Defaults for a type go in Config.PropertyTypes . Fields ¶ Field What it does label The name shown on prompts, blips and in logs. price What it costs. Leave out for a property that can't be bought (e.g. a government building handed out by command). coords Where the buy prompt is. Defaults to the first door. doors The doors to lock. See Doors . storage A stash. See Storage . blip Overrides the type's blip. A table with any of sprite , label , coords , forSale , owned , mine , or false for no blip. See Blips . lockable false for a property whose doors are never locked. Default true . lockpick Lockpicking for every door (and the storage) of this property: false for key only, or a table of minigame settings for a harder lock. Default true . storageLockpick Lockpicking for the storage only, overriding lockpick and Config.Lockpick.storage . keyItem The key item for this property. Defaults to the type's, then Config.KeyItem . storagePrefix The storage's inventory id is storagePrefix .. key (e.g. houseID_57858 ). Without one it's the id with : swapped for _ . Usually set per type, to keep an older script's inventories. minGrade For a property owned by a job: the lowest grade that gets in. Default 0 . Other scripts can read their own fields from the same entry. tr-ranching, for example, uses: Field What it does area The middle of the ranch's land ( vector3 ); animals that wander too far escape. animals How many animals the ranch can hold. Doors ¶ Each door is keyed by its door hash. The simple form is a vector4 of the door's position and its closed heading: doors = { [ 1535511805 ] = vector4 ( - 2590.84 , 457.84 , 146.01 , - 100.23 ), }, For options, use a table: doors = { [ 1234567890 ] = vector4 ( x , y , z , h ), -- lockable, can be picked [ 2345678901 ] = { coords = vector4 ( x , y , z , h ), lockpick = { pins = 5 } }, -- a harder lock [ 3456789012 ] = { coords = vector4 ( x , y , z , h ), lockpick = false }, -- key only [ 4567890123 ] = { coords = vector4 ( x , y , z , h ), lockable = false }, -- always open [ 2917406796 ] = { coords = vector4 ( x , y , z , h ), model = "p_door44x" }, -- an MLO door (below) }, Door field What it does coords Position and closed heading ( vector4 ). A door's position is its hinge. lockable false keeps this door open. lockpick false for key only, or minigame settings. Defaults to the property's. model For doors the game's door system can't lock (some MLO doors): the door's model. The door prop is then held shut directly. See Setting up a new door . Only list outside doors (and interior doors you want locked, like an office). Doors you leave out aren't touched. Storage ¶ storage = { coords = vector3 ( - 1317.91 , 2454.16 , 310 ), weight = 500 , radius = 1.5 , lockpick = { pins = 6 } }, Storage field What it does coords Where the Open Storage prompt is. weight How much it holds. Default 500 . radius How close the player needs to be. Default 1.5 . lockpick false for key only, or minigame settings. See Lockpicking . Storage only works for types listed in Config.Storage , and only once the property is owned. Anyone carrying a key that fits can open it.

docs.text: Keys ¶ Buying a property gives the buyer a key. Every key carries the serial of the lock it fits, and each property has one lock at a time. Using a key at a door locks or unlocks that door, if the key fits. Only the key used counts, not others in the player's pockets. Storage and blips count any fitting key the player carries. Changing the locks gives the property a new lock. Every old key stops working. If a player's inventory is full when they buy, nothing is charged and they're asked to make room. If a key copy or lock change won't fit, the materials are given back and the old lock stays. Locksmiths ¶ A player with one of Config.Locksmith.jobs can: Copy a key by using it at one of Config.Locksmith.locations . Costs Config.Locksmith.cost . Change the locks with /changelocks at the door, with the owner standing next to them. The locksmith gets the new key. Other scripts can do the same through the exports (tr-government's office uses them). Lockpicking ¶ Using a lockpick near a door, or a storage, starts the lockpick minigame: Success on a door flips that one door: locked becomes unlocked, and unlocked becomes locked. Success on storage opens it once. Nothing stays unlocked. Failure uses up the lockpick (unless removeOnFail is off). Doors on unowned properties can be picked too. They lock themselves again after Config.Lockpick.relockUnowned minutes, and on restart. Every attempt is logged, and fires an event alert scripts can listen to (see For developers ). Whether a lock can be picked, and how hard, comes from the first of these that's set: The door's or storage's own lockpick The property's storageLockpick (storage only) Config.Lockpick.storage (storage only) The property's (or its type's) lockpick false means key only. A table of minigame settings is laid over Config.Lockpick.minigame , so it only needs what's different, e.g. { pins = 5 } . Setting up a new door ¶ Turn on Config.Debug and stand at the door: /doorcheck <hash> prints whether the game's door system knows the door. If entity is 0 or false , it can't lock it; give the door a model . Close the door and run /doorscan . It lists every object within 4 metres. Find the door's model and its heading. /doorlook prints the object you're looking at, if /doorscan lists too much. Then add the door with its closed heading: [ 2917406796 ] = { coords = vector4 ( 1250.61 , 1156.41 , 150.23 , - 59.79 ), model = "p_door44x" }, The heading is the closed one Locking turns the door to this heading before holding it. A wrong heading holds the door open at an angle. Admin ¶ /property (ACE-restricted, also works from the server console): Command What it does /property <id> owner char <charid> Gives the property to a character. /property <id> owner job <job> Gives the property to a job. /property <id> release Puts it back on the market. /property <id> lock / unlock Locks or unlocks every door. /property <id> key Gives you a key to it. Changing an owner by command doesn't hand out a key; use key and give it to them.

docs.text: tr-properties keeps the ownership, keys and doors; your script adds what's specific to it. tr-housing and tr-ranching are built this way. Server exports ¶ local props = exports [ "tr-properties" ] Export Returns What it does register(id, data) Adds a property, in the same format as the config. get(id) table or nil label , type , price , coords , lockable , storage , owner , locked , plus area and animals . getOwner(id) { kind, id } or nil kind is "char" or "job" . getOwned(kind, ownerId) list of ids Every property a character or job owns. getForSale(type?) list of ids Unowned properties with a price, optionally of one type. hasAccess(src, id, ignoreLock?) boolean Owner, job member, master job or a fitting key. isOwner(src, id) boolean The owning character, or a member of the owning job. setLocked(id, locked, hash?) boolean Locks or unlocks one door, or every door without a hash. purchase(src, id) ok, err Charges the price and gives the property and key, with all the usual checks. transfer(id, owner, src?) boolean Gives the property to owner ( { kind, id } ). src gets the new key. release(id) boolean Puts the property back on the market. giveKey(src, id) key serial or false A key to the current lock. false if not owned or no room. changeLocks(id, src) ok, err A new lock, with its first key to src . Keeps the old lock if the key doesn't fit. setProvider(name, value) Takes over part of the script. See Providers . Client exports ¶ Export What it does get(id) The property as the client sees it (label, doors and their lock states, storage, blip...). canAccess(id) Asks the server whether this player can get in. addStorageOption(type, label, key, onSelect) Adds a prompt next to Open Storage for every property of a type. onSelect(id) runs when it's pressed. hideStorage(hidden) Hides the storage prompt, e.g. while a menu opened from it is up. exports [ "tr-properties" ]: addStorageOption ( "house" , "Open Wardrobe" , "INPUT_INTERACT_OPTION2" , function ( id ) OpenWardrobe () end ) Storage options are lost when tr-properties restarts. Add them again on onClientResourceStart : AddEventHandler ( "onClientResourceStart" , function ( resource ) if resource == "tr-properties" then addOptions () end end ) Events ¶ Server events, for scripts that react to properties: Event Arguments When tr-properties:ownerChanged id, owner, previous Bought, transferred or released. owner is nil when released. tr-properties:lockChanged id, locked, hash A door (or every door, hash = nil ) was locked or unlocked. tr-properties:storageOpened src, id A player opened a property's storage with a key. tr-properties:lockpicked src, id, hash, success, target A lockpick attempt. target is "door" or "storage" ; hash is nil for storage. Providers ¶ A provider replaces one part of the script. Set it from your script when it starts: exports [ "tr-properties" ]: setProvider ( "sale" , "external" ) -- no buying at the door Provider Default What it does sale "door" "external" turns off the buy prompt, for scripts that sell properties themselves (e.g. a government office calling purchase ). pay cash function(src, amount) : take the price. Return true if paid. refund cash function(src, amount) : give the price back when a purchase can't finish. Set sale back to "door" when your script stops, so properties can still be bought.

docs.text: A door says it's locked but stays open ¶ The game's door system doesn't know the door, which happens with some MLO doors. Run /doorcheck <hash> (with Config.Debug on): if entity is 0 or false , give the door a model . See Setting up a new door . A locked door stands open at an angle ¶ The door's heading is wrong. Look for a SCRIPT ERROR from tr-properties in the server console, and check that oxmysql started first. Bought a property but got no key ¶ The player's inventory was full. Nothing is charged in that case and they're told to make room. For properties given by command, use /property <id> key . Using a key says it doesn't fit ¶ The locks were changed since that key was cut, or it's a key to another property. The key's description shows its lock serial. docs.text: A highly customisable script for "rumors": places on the map that players find out about by overhearing locals. How it works ¶ When a player passes within earshot of a local ( Config.distance , 2.0 by default), they have a chance ( Config.chance , 20% by default) to overhear a rumor , and that place is marked on their map. Rumors can be about anything: crime, secret places, legendary animals, and more. By default, a rumor comes with a vague map marker (an area rather than an exact point) that disappears after a while (5 minutes by default). Players can start their own rumors too: set a waypoint on the map, then use /startrumor . Rumors last until the script or server restarts. Requirements ¶ jo_libs License ¶ This script is free to use, and you can change your copy of the source code freely.

docs.text: Adding a rumor ¶ A registered rumor can be overheard at random near locals: -- TriggerEvent("tr-rumors:RegisterLocation", name, coords, options) TriggerEvent ( "tr-rumors:RegisterLocation" , "LegendaryAnimal" , coords ) Forcing a rumor on a player ¶ A rumor can also be put straight on a player's map. It has to be registered first. -- exports["tr-rumors"]:ForceRumor(player, name, options) exports [ "tr-rumors" ]: ForceRumor ( data . source , "LegendaryAnimal" ) Customising a rumor ¶ Both take an optional options table. Anything you set replaces the default from Config.options , and anything you leave out keeps the default: TriggerEvent ( "tr-rumors:RegisterLocation" , "myRumor" , vector3 ( 0 , 0 , 0 ), { radius = 10 , blip = { label = "Custom Rumor" , }, notification = { title = "This is a custom rumor. Anything left out uses the default!" , }, }) A forced rumor can look different from the registered one: TriggerEvent ( "tr-rumors:RegisterLocation" , "LegendaryAnimal" , coords ) exports [ "tr-rumors" ]: ForceRumor ( data . source , "LegendaryAnimal" , { blip = { label = "Legendary Animal" , modifiers = { "BLIP_MODIFIER_MP_COLOR_5" , "BLIP_MODIFIER_FLASH_MEDIUM" , "BLIP_MODIFIER_MP_OVERLAY_ANIMAL" , }, }, notification = { title = "A legendary animal has been sighted!" , dict = "toasts_mp_generic" , icon = "toast_mp_animal" , }, }) To use the defaults, leave options out or pass an empty table: TriggerEvent ( "tr-rumors:RegisterLocation" , "myRumor" , vector3 ( 0 , 0 , 0 )) exports [ "tr-rumors" ]: ForceRumor ( player , "myRumor" )

docs.text: Put the tr-wild-horses folder in your server's resources folder. Change any settings, spawn groups or spawn areas you want in overwriteConfig.lua . Restart the server, or run refresh and then ensure tr-wild-horses . The script comes ready to use, so step 2 is optional.

docs.text: It only adds spawns ¶ The script doesn't change any of the game's own spawn points. It only adds new spawn areas around the places in the config, and does nothing but spawn horses near the player, so it should work alongside any other script. One horse per area, per player ¶ It runs on each player's game, so it spawns at most one horse per area per player , and doesn't limit the total. Two players in the same spawn area can see up to two horses, one each (depending on the spawn chance). Horses can be hard to find ¶ Spawn areas are large (100.0 by default), and a horse can appear anywhere inside one, sometimes somewhere odd, like up on a cliff. If that's a problem, make the areas smaller (25 or 50, adjusting the spawn distance from the player to match) and lower the spawn chance. Horses are then easier to find once they spawn, but spawn less often.
